# GEMSDOE77 review — branch `arena/705c4339-gemsdoe77` — 2026-10-21

## Decision at a glance

**No new GeoTIFF was generated by this review. No new experiment was run. No weekly competition slot was used.** This invocation assigned no identifiable method paragraph. A fresh candidate-independent preflight under the user's literal overlap rule proves every nonempty allowed prediction has a duplicate witness.

**Submission status is conflicted; do not upload under this review.** The aggregate machine-readable release gate says `NOT OK TO SUBMIT` and `0` authorized files. After the concurrent mainline merge, the README and H85 lane carry an operator-level “OK TO SUBMIT” / “PROMOTE” claim, but the same aggregate receipt records `certified_by_gate: false`, the registry scan is incomplete, `approved_for_weekly_slot: false`, and no slot was spent. More importantly, direct readback of H85's TIFF shows literal 3-px forward overlap `1.0` against the pinned full-support witness, exceeding the user's explicit `0.70` stop rule. The H85 local amendment excludes space-filling priors from its binding comparison; this review does not apply that exception because it conflicts with the present prompt. This is a documented policy/provenance irregularity, not an organizer decision. See `docs/irregularities.md` (IR-705-H85-01).

### Pass 3 — original request, score interpretation, and safety

#### What can and cannot be said about the reported H33 `0.2778`

The value `0.2778` for `h33-h33-2-b2-20261004T220000Z-e5eb6e7e-zeros` remains **OWNER-REPORT**, not an `ORGANIZER-CONFIRMED` file-to-score receipt. The repository's pinned H33 analysis reports byte forensics consistent with pruning 6,436 near-catalogue pixels from a 44,090-pixel predecessor, leaving 37,654; those are raster measurements, not competition scores. It also records that the GEMSDOE32 page itself states that no organizer score exists for its listed artifact.

A plausible mechanism—not causal proof—is that thinning and near-catalogue pruning reduce redundant prediction mass under an asymmetric distance-weighted Tversky objective while retaining useful coverage of hidden faults. It can help only when the removed mass contributes little to hidden truth; the same operation can hurt if removed dots were useful. The exact marginal-coverage term depends on maximum kernel credit across truth pixels, so there is no generally valid fixed per-dot penalty or universal distance threshold. `research/why-h33-scored-02778.md` derives the correct condition and tests counterexamples against the pinned implementation.

Therefore: **why H33 scored 0.2778 is not established from the evidence available here; the sparse/pruned-field explanation is a defensible hypothesis.** Whether a distinct method can beat that owner-reported number is unknown. A holdout improvement is necessary for promotion under the project protocol, but it is neither an organizer leaderboard score nor proof of geothermal productivity. The brief's `0.3195` and repo notes referring to `0.4413` conflict as current targets; no live leaderboard value was verified in this review.

## Ranked research hypotheses — proposals only, not validated or authorized

Priority is qualitative expected scientific signal per implementation cost; expected DTI gain is **unknown**, and no score projection is made. “Not found” means only that a targeted search of this repository's code/research did not reveal that specific operator; global or cross-repository novelty is not claimed. All remain blocked until the shared uniqueness policy is resolved and an authorized lane is assigned.

| Rank | Layers and targeted physical signature | Why it may locate a catalogue-missing fault | Named non-fault mimic | Difference from work found in this repo; cost/readiness |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Competition GeoDAWN RTP/TMI and isostatic gravity bands, with depth-to-basement: **multi-scale cross-wavelet phase-jump persistence co-located with a signed basement-depth step**. | A buried offset under basin fill may produce a persistent cross-field phase/contact break and throw without a mappable surface scarp; a multi-scale phase criterion is intended to discount isolated amplitude edges. | Intrusive/lithologic contacts, caldera margins, flight-line seams, and mismatched gridding. | Distinctive operator is cross-scale wavelet phase persistence plus signed depth-step gating, rather than H83-PCD's Poisson pseudogravity–gravity discordance/piedmont toe, H82-GMNS's network-mechanics allocator, amplitude ridge, or a single-scale gradient. This is a materially different test (phase concordance plus throw sign), but remains only a proposal. Medium cost. It uses competition/GeoDAWN layers in principle, but those full rasters are absent from this checkout; no holdout was run. **Blocked, not viable in this invocation.** |
| 2 | USGS 3DEP DEM plus derived drainage graph and catchments: **fault-parallel channel deflection and paired knickzone/normalized-steepness breaks repeated in adjacent catchments**. | Distributed warping or small offsets can perturb several channels after a local scarp is degraded or buried, exposing a structure missing from a surface-trace catalogue. | Lithologic resistance boundaries, stream capture, alluvial-fan avulsion, roads or irrigation. | Network/topology-level channel relationships are different from the repo's pixelwise scarp, curvature, step, and knickpoint features. High DEM-conditioning cost. Specific official free source: [USGS 3DEP](https://www.usgs.gov/3d-elevation-program). This source and exact AOI tile obtainability were not checked from this sandbox; therefore **not viable until availability is verified**. |
| 3 | USGS ComCat FDSN event locations and focal mechanisms, with competition depth-to-basement/geophysical context: **uncertainty-weighted 3-D event-plane alignment projected up-dip**. | A blind active structure may host a planar microseismicity cluster at depth without a surface scarp or existing mapped trace. | Volcanic/geothermal swarm, aftershock sequence, quarry blast, and spatially variable network detection. | Discrete event-plane fitting is distinct from coarse smoothed seismicity bands already in the feature stack. High data/QC cost. Specific free official source: [USGS ComCat FDSN event service](https://earthquake.usgs.gov/fdsnws/event/1/query). Prior repository checks record the host as outside this sandbox's egress allowlist; no source retrieval is claimed here. **Not viable in this invocation.** |
| 4 | Competition GeoDAWN K/Th/U and total-count bands: **local empirical-copula change points along boundaries persistent across neighboring windows and scales**. | Joint radiometric texture change may reveal alteration/contact zones over a fault not represented by a single-band threshold or topographic scarp. | Soil moisture, grain sorting, vegetation/cover, lithologic boundary, and survey seams. | Distributional dependence/change-point evidence, not the previously explored single-channel U curvature, entropy, or simple pairwise ratio. Medium cost. It relies on missing local GeoDAWN rasters and may overlap scientific scope with earlier radiometric lanes; no independent novelty or holdout gain is asserted. **Blocked in this invocation.** |

1. Ask the shared protocol owner to resolve the literal 3-px uniqueness/support rule against the pinned all-domain witness. Do not carve out dense rasters locally or patch a private evaluator.
2. Obtain the missing competition feature raster and any required DEMs from an authorized, verifiable source; preserve provenance as either organizer-authenticated or owner-mirrored, never conflate them. Confirm current portal rules/weekly cap through an authenticated submission page.
3. Receive a specific method-paragraph lane assignment; search prior work and preregister one candidate before any experiment. Budget at most three experiments/two hours.
4. Only if shared uniqueness can be passed, restore the cached stack, run feature-alone leakage canaries, perform buffered whole-segment hide-and-recover with catalogue-derived features built only from visible segments and exact masking, and compare pooled DTI plus 95% CI to a matched incumbent. Use the pinned evaluator/writer.
5. Generate a TIFF only if the locked holdout criterion improves, pre-placement surface and final-dot registry gates pass, all grid/range/hash validations pass, and the separate selector approves. Record portal acceptance only from an actual receipt.
6. Simplify the historical site navigation/status archive after preserving its reproducibility; several top-level README/site sections refer to other branches and can distract from the operative fail-closed state.
